original_summary: Two young hunters become lost in remote mountains after a failed expedition and enter an attractive restaurant that promises to welcome its guests. Inside, they encounter a series of increasingly odd instructions, each presented as part of the preparation for an excellent meal. Their hunger and confidence lead them to comply, even as the instructions begin to suggest that they—not an animal—are being prepared as food. At last, they understand the danger and react with genuine fear.
seed_elements: Two companions are isolated in a hostile wilderness after a disappointing journey.
They find a welcoming building that offers comfort, food, and apparent safety.
A sequence of polite but disturbing instructions gradually reveals a hidden threat.
Hunger, pride, and wishful thinking keep the characters obeying despite growing unease.
The central reversal is discovering that the guests are the intended prey.
discarded_elements: Kenji Miyazawa’s name and the original Japanese title
The 1924 publication era and historical source details
The hunters’ British-soldier-style clothing and specific weapons
The original mountain geography and period-specific hunting context
The restaurant’s exact sequence of rooms, notices, and final details
Any original character names or incidental descriptive details
conversion_plan: Modernize the story as a third-person English-learning tale about two hikers or stranded travelers who find an isolated smart lodge, wellness retreat, or roadside restaurant. Use short sentences, clear dialogue, and a steadily escalating pattern of instructions, with accessible vocabulary for an intermediate audience. Aim for roughly 1,000–1,500 words, preserving the uneasy humor and final realization while creating new characters, setting details, and wording.
